# Routarr

> Routarr is a self-hosted routing and classification layer for Radarr and Sonarr. It reads their
> libraries, enriches every film and series from metadata sources in an order the user sets,
> evaluates rules the user writes, and moves each title to the right root folder through the Arr
> API. It shows the whole plan first and writes only when the user says so.

It ships as one Docker image for amd64 and arm64, so a Pi or an N100 is enough. Storage is a
single SQLite file, with no database service to run. It is licensed GPL-3.0-only and is not
affiliated with the Servarr project.

Routarr never manages downloads, indexers or the library itself, and it does not replace Radarr
or Sonarr. A move writes exactly two things through the Arr API, the root folder and the path,
then asks for a rescan. The folder name stays as it is, so a library that Plex or Jellyfin reads
keeps working.

It works in four steps, and only the last one writes to the library:

1. Sync reads films, series, tags and root folders from every connected Radarr and Sonarr. An
   empty response is never treated as a mass deletion.
2. Enrich writes only to Routarr's own cache. Genres, original language and certification come
   with the sync. TMDb and AniList add keywords and origin country.
3. Decide runs the rules by ascending priority, and the first match wins. Exclusions veto a rule
   that otherwise matched, and a title no rule matches falls to the default category. The result
   is a plan the user can read.
4. Apply groups the moves per instance and target folder, writes them through the Arr API, then
   asks for a rescan. Every applied move can be reverted.

A rule combines conditions with ALL or ANY, can carry explicit exclusions, has a priority, and
routes to a category. The 28 conditions include genre, keywords, language, country,
certification, age, size, paths, tags, Sonarr's series type and season count. The impact of a
rule can be previewed before it is saved. An override pins a title to a category and outranks
every rule. For every title, the explanation shows what each condition expected and what it
observed, for the winning rule and for every rule that did not win.

The user names the categories and attaches root folders to them. A root folder is either one
that Radarr or Sonarr reports or one declared in Routarr, and a declared folder takes its free
space and reachability from the synced folder it sits under. Routarr never creates a library
layout.

Six gates run in this order before anything is written, and the first to object stops the rest:
global dry-run, batch cap, reachability, capacity, confirmation threshold, and revalidation at
apply time. All six are on by default. The global dry-run is on from the first launch, blocks
writes at the server whatever the interface does, and alone makes the whole application
read-only. Reachability, capacity and the confirmation threshold ask the user a question, and
the other three refuse. Moving files on disk is an option, unchecked by default. Without it,
Routarr re-points the library entry and leaves the files where they are. Automatic application
exists and is off by default. When enabled, it touches only titles with no files on disk yet.

Metadata sources form an ordered list, and the order decides which source wins when they
disagree. No metadata key is required: Radarr and Sonarr are a source of their own, and AniList
and Jikan need no key. TMDb, OMDb and TheTVDB are optional.

Routarr also provides:

- Any number of Radarr and Sonarr instances, each with its own sync interval, folders and
  mappings.
- A secret webhook URL per instance. A title added in Radarr or Sonarr is synced, enriched and
  evaluated at once rather than at the next poll, and can be routed before it downloads.
- Authentication on by default: an API key, a single account, or OpenID Connect.
- Prometheus metrics at /metrics, behind the same API key.
- Notifications through one generic JSON webhook for Discord, Gotify, ntfy or Apprise, fired on
  a state change.
- A backup into data/backups/ every day, unless the interval is changed.
- Export of rules, categories, mappings and overrides as JSON. Arr API keys are encrypted at rest
  with AES-256-GCM and are left out of the export.
- Translations into 26 languages, decision justifications included.

It has no telemetry, no analytics and no update check. Its only outbound calls go to the
configured Radarr and Sonarr instances, to the metadata sources the user enables, to an OpenID
Connect provider if one is used, and to a notification webhook if one is set.

To install, save the compose file from the README (image ghcr.io/routarr/routarr:latest, port
9876, ./data mounted at /data) and run:

```bash
mkdir -p data && sudo chown 1000:1000 data
docker compose up -d
docker exec routarr cat /data/routarr.api_key
```

The last command prints the API key generated on first start. Open http://localhost:9876 and
paste it. The container runs as uid 1000 and drops every capability, so the data directory has
to belong to uid 1000. Back up the whole data/ directory: without routarr.key, the stored Arr
credentials cannot be recovered. The image tag latest follows the most recent release, 0.1
follows the patch releases of 0.1, and a full version such as 0.1.0 pins one.

First use, in the interface: Instances (add Radarr or Sonarr, test the connection, sync), Root
Folders (create categories, map folders to them, declare any destination the Arrs do not list),
Rules (write rules and preview their impact), Simulation (run it, read the justifications, apply
what you agree with), and Settings (turn off the global dry-run once the result is trusted).

ROUTARR_AUTH selects authentication: apikey (the default), forms (one account with a password),
oidc (OpenID Connect), external (a reverse proxy in front authenticates) or none (open).
ROUTARR_BASE_PATH serves Routarr under a sub-path such as /routarr behind a reverse proxy. The
API, the interface and the webhook URLs all move with it, and no image rebuild is needed.
ROUTARR_API_KEY sets the API key instead of generating one, and ROUTARR_SECRET_KEY sets the key
that encrypts the stored Arr keys. Every variable is listed in backend/.env.example, and
everything else is set from the Settings page.

Security issues are reported privately through GitHub, as SECURITY.md describes, never in a
public issue. Only the most recent release is supported. Out of scope by design: a permission
model (there is one level of access), telemetry of any kind (opt-in included), a second database
engine, signal weighting, nested condition groups, temporary overrides and a persistent job
queue.

The Site links below are the two English pages of the showcase site, and their French, German
and Spanish copies are under Optional. Under Docs, repository files are linked as raw text, and
the README is the reference for installation and configuration.

## Site

- [Landing page](https://routarr.app/): what Routarr does, with an example dry-run plan, a rule,
  the six gates and the install steps.
- [How it decides](https://routarr.app/how/): the gap Routarr fills, the four steps, how a
  decision is explained, how root folders are declared, the full specification, and the
  objections answered.

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Routarr/Routarr/main/README.md): features, quick
  start, image tags, configuration and backups.
- [Environment variables](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Routarr/Routarr/main/backend/.env.example):
  every variable, listed and commented, OpenID Connect and the metadata source keys included.
- [Security policy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Routarr/Routarr/main/SECURITY.md): how to
  report a vulnerability, which versions are supported, what is already in place, and the known
  limits.
- [Contributing guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Routarr/Routarr/main/CONTRIBUTING.md):
  the development setup, the checks CI runs, commit conventions, the release process, and what
  will be turned down.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/Routarr/Routarr): code, issues and releases.
